articles.title: Jacksonville Jaguars 33-10 Baltimore Ravens: Joe Fagnano throws two interceptions as Ravens suffer heavy loss
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens' third quarterback of the season, rookie Joe Fagnano, throws for just 60 yards and two interceptions in his first NFL start as the Baltimore Ravens (4-5) suffer a fourth straight loss at home to the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) on Thursday night
articles.body:
Fagnano came in due to Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley both being injured, with the 25-year-old rookie finding things a big struggle as Baltimore (4-5) lost a fourth straight on the season.

With their top two quarterbacks on injured reserve, the Ravens now await Jacoby Brissett's arrival in a trade from the Arizona Cardinals as they try to prevent their season from falling apart.

Jacksonville (6-2) did not need to do anything extraordinary to beat a badly weakened Baltimore team. Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown as the Jags won their fifth in their last six to take further command of the AFC South.

Passing: Trevor Lawrence, 16/26, 242 yards, 1 TD

Rushing: Ameer Abdullah, 7 carries, 30 yards

Receiving: Jakobi Meyers, 4 catches, 65 yards

Passing: Joe Fagnano, 10/18, 60 yards, 2 INTs

Rushing: Justice Hill, 9 carries, 85 yards, 1 TD

Receiving: Mark Andrews, 2 catches, 19 yards

Jacksonville drove 77 yards on the game's first possession, taking a 7-0 advantage on a one-yard touchdown run by Bhayshul Tuten.

The Ravens tried to be creative, repeatedly running Wildcat-style plays where running back Derrick Henry took direct snaps. They managed a field goal on their first drive but nothing more for much of the matchup.

It was still competitive up until the end of the first half, when Lawrence found Parker Washington for a 50-yard scoring strike with 58 seconds left in the second quarter to make the score 17-3.

It was 20-3 when a fumble gave Baltimore the ball at midfield in the third quarter, but the Ravens immediately turned the ball over on downs and the boos came cascading down from the home crowd.

Fagnano went 10 of 18 with two second-half interceptions. Baltimore also lost a fumble on a kick return, which led to Chris Rodriguez Jr's two-yard touchdown run with just over seven minutes left in the game that made it 33-3.

Justice Hill broke free for a 65-yard touchdown run 11 seconds later - Baltimore's first TD after half-time since Week 5. He finished with 85 yards and that score on nine carries.

articles.title: Real Madrid's Bernabeu welcomes back NFL as Joe Burrow leads Cincinnati Bengals' Super Bowl hunt - NFL Gameday Guide
articles.summary: MVP contender Joe Burrow leads the Cincinnati Bengals out against the Atlanta Falcons at Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium, live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm on Sunday; the game is followed by Denver Broncos against Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers versus New England Patriots
articles.body:
Only one thing is more exciting and more celebrated than a Jude Bellingham Calvin Klein commercial in Madrid this week. No, not Duran Duran's live show on Friday night.

Of course, we are talking about the NFL's return to Spain, where Bellingham and Real Madrid's iconic Bernabeu opens its doors to gridiron for a second straight year when the Cincinnati Bengals take on the Atlanta Falcons in the resumption of football's European roadtrip this Sunday.

Madrid will take centre stage once again for the seventh of a record nine international games being played in 2026, arriving a fortnight on from the NFL's Paris debut and ahead of its return to Munich later this month. In doing so it welcomes an MVP and Super Bowl contender to town, so too perhaps the best running back in the sport.

As for the aforementioned MVP candidate, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow arrives armed with a growing Super Bowl impatience as he and Zac Taylor seek to cash in on one of the league's borderline-unstoppable offenses. He has tasted Lombardi heartbreak, he has endured post-Big Dance hangovers and weathered both the mental and physical impact of contention-hindering injury setbacks. But he has momentum and a long-awaited fast start with which to launch Cincinnati's Championship surge.

Burrow was blunt in the offseason of the need for urgency, placing a 'this is it' last-chance-saloon pressure on his own organisation in view of a Super Bowl run. He has answered his own call emphatically with chart-topping numbers over the first half of the campaign.

The former No 1 overall pick is 195 of 267 passing with a league-high completion percentage of 73 while amassing 2,115 yards and a league-high 20 touchdowns to six interceptions. His 302.1 yards per game are the most in the NFL, he leads all quarterbacks with a success rate of 55.3 and is first in completion percentage over expected.

"He's playing his best football that he has ever played in his career in my opinion right now," said Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich.

To put into context the dominance of both Burrow and Cincinnati's No 1-ranked passing attack, the Bengals are seventh in total yards and second in scoring despite ranking 30th in the running game. In fact, the Bengals have posted just one run of 15 or more yards this season, the fewest in the league.

It has been uncontainable aerial bombardment, Tee Higgins second only to Jaxon Smith-Njigba with 726 receiving yards while Ja'Marr Chase has 492 yards. There isn't a more explosive or more frightening offensive trip currently, and as much has always meant that Cincinnati's search for defensive improvement need not be transformative, but merely enough to float somewhere around middle ground.

"Usually a team kind of has one number one guy and they have two of them," said Falcons safety Xavier Watts of Higgins and Chase. "It is a unique opportunity and challenge and we'll have to prepare adjustments and game plans to try to take away both of them, but it's a great opportunity."

A Burrow at his best hides a team's weaknesses as well as any quarterback. The 2026 Burrow is flirting with something close to a Burrow at his best.

Burrow just threw for 462 passing yards and five touchdowns before rushing for the deciding score in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans, overcoming three interceptions - all to Amani Hooker - in the process to reassert his box office promise. It made him the fifth quarterback since 2000 to record at least five touchdown passes and three interceptions in one game.

He, Chase and Higgins is why the Bengals can afford to make life difficult for themselves. Though a real Championship contender would prefer to play from the front.

Madrid is getting one of football's legitimate superstars, leading a legitimate Super Bowl contender four years on from their runner-up disappointment against the Los Angeles Rams. And yes, the prospective MVP wears Pokemon outfits in which to fly.

Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard just raced to 117 yards and two touchdowns on the ground in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals, while Cam Ward collected 41 using his feet. While Dexter Lawrence has fortified a much-maligned defense, it is a unit that still raises question marks as to its Championship pedigree. As mentioned before, not every team has the luxury of a Burrow with which to survive a shootout should they need to.

On Sunday, they meet the NFL's leading rusher in Bijan Robinson, who tops the chats with 780 yards on the ground despite failing to produce upwards of 86 in each of the last four games. Is it a coincidence that Atlanta have lost three of their last four? Perhaps not. When he sizzles, the Falcons tend to be a threat to anybody.

Jared Goff may not be the sexy pick, but the Detroit Lions quarterback is deserving of a place in the early MVP discussion. He has started the season 168 of 248 (67.7 per cent) passing for 1,964 yards (seventh-most) at 280.6 yards per game (third-most) for 15 touchdowns to just one interception with a fourth-ranked passer rating of 110.0. He has been phenomenal as a pilot to the No 1-ranked offense in football in total yards, and yet he may not be the MVP of his own team.

The Lions are witnessing another standout year from running back Jahmyr Gibbs, whose 773 rushing yards are second only to Robinson's 780 in one game less, and his 1,058 scrimmage yards first in the NFL. He has scored 10 total touchdowns - tied for first with D'Andre Swift - has touched the ball a league-high 191 times, is averaging a league-high 110.4 rushing yards per game, and has more first down runs than any back in football. He is the Lions offense, and just bolstered his case for individual honours - more likely to be Offensive Player of the Year come January - by wearing down Brian Flores' famed Minnesota Vikings defense. Unstoppable.

"I'd run it," said Todd Bowles in response to the heavy Tampa rainfall. Run it he did. The Buccaneers made history last weekend by beating the Falcons 16-0 as the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a pass, Baker Mayfield finishing zero of three through the air while playing more as an extra blocker than as a quarterback.

Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell combined for 310 yards from 52 carries on the ground while Tampa were assisted by four Michael Penix Jr interceptions. Irving is up to fourth in the NFL with 728 yards as the focal point to an offense ranked No 1 in rushing. They and their No 2-ranked rushing defense will now take on the Chicago Bears and their No 2-ranked rushing offense in a collision of ground control, D'Andre Swift leading the way with 545 yards for a league-leading 10 touchdowns.

The Bears are coming off a statement win over the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, the rise of Caleb Williams to MVP pursuer and the introduction of Jeffery Simmons seeing Ben Johnson's side cut the figure of serious challengers.

It may not be pretty, it may not be good for the heart-rate, but the Denver Broncos find a way. It is their DNA, it is what they do and it is why they can win a Super Bowl under Sean Payton.

They did it again on Sunday with a dramatic goalline stand to deny the Kansas City Chiefs and cap their comeback from an 11-point deficit to win 28-24. It would mean they have now won 15 straight regular season games decided by one score, tied with the 2008-09 Indianapolis Colts for the longest streak in history. What's more, it marked Bo Nix's 13th fourth-quarterback comeback win, the most by a quarterback in his first three seasons since 1950.

With J.K. Dobbins not getting it done, the Broncos have unearthed a new asset out of the backfield in fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman, who had 104 yards and one touchdown from 15 scrimmage touches against the Chiefs. Nor Nix or this Broncos offense is lighting up the world, and yet here they are at 6-2 and looking difficult to beat.

The Packers witnessed the brilliant best and excruciating worst of Matthew Golden in last Thursday's win over the Carolina Panthers. On one play, Golden burned his defender with a fake high-and-go route only to inexcusably drop a wide-open touchdown; a play later, Jordan Love went right back to his receiver, who this time broke free to haul in a 24-yard touchdown catch on third-and-13.

The second-year wideout is guilty of an NFL-most nine drops this season, while the Packers as a team have a league-leading 23 through eight games, according to Pro Football Focus. Still, Matt LaFleur's passing offense ranks second in the NFL as it continues to compensate for a ground game sitting dead last, Love carrying his team with a league-high 2,246 passing yards for 16 touchdowns to six interceptions, albeit while completing just 61.5 of passes.

The Ravens placed quarterback Lamar Jackson on injured reserve due to a thumb injury that requires surgery; Baltimore subsequently traded for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett.

Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons returned to practice for the first time since suffering an ACL tear against the Broncos last December.

The Saints cut kicker Daniel Carlson, meaning Irish kicker Charlie Smyth will start against the Cleveland Browns this weekend.

Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold was ruled out of his side's clash with the Cardinals due to a quad injury and a cracked rib, with Drew Lock primed to start.

The Jaguars kicked off Week Nine with a commanding 33-10 win over the Ravens, who were led by third-string undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano.

Bills quarterback Josh Allen needs just nine rushing yards against the Vikings to join Lamar Jackson (6,666 rushing yards), Michael Vick (6,109), Cam Newton (5,628) and Russell Wilson (5,568) as the only quarterbacks in NFL history with at least 5,000 rushing yards.

Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes needs three touchdown passes to surpass Peyton Manning (327) for the most by a player in his first 10 seasons, including playoffs, in NFL history.

Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs needs just one more scrimmage touchdown to become the third player with at least 60 touchdowns in his first four seasons in NFL history behind Terrell Davis and LaDainian Tomlinson.

A touchdown catch in Madrid would see Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase join Randy Moss as the only players in NFL history with at least seven touchdown catches in each of his first six seasons

49ers tight end George Kittle needs 75 receiving yards to join Rob Gronkowski as the only tight ends in NFL history with at least 500 receiving yards in each of his first 10 seasons.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's ankle injury takes an unexpected turn as Chiefs get encouraging sign before Week 9 showdown
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has given the Kansas City Chiefs a welcome injury boost ahead of their Week 9 game.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has given the Kansas City Chiefs a welcome injury boost ahead of their Week 9 game. The veteran tight end, who has been managing an ankle problem since the Week 7 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, returned to full participation in Thursday's practice, November 5. That is a significant change from Wednesday's injury report, when Kelce was still limited. His latest update offers hope that Patrick Mahomes will have his most dependable receiving option available this weekend, although Friday's practice report will provide another indication of his status.Travis Kelce's full participation offers Chiefs a major injury boostThe Chiefs had reason to keep a close eye on Travis Kelce after his ankle injury against the Chargers in Week 7. He continued to play despite the issue, but his practice schedule suggested that the problem had not completely gone away.Kelce was limited on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday during the following week. He has also had to manage his workload during recent practices, making his latest participation particularly encouraging for Kansas City.On Wednesday, November 4, the tight end was once again listed as a limited participant. That raised some concern about whether the ankle was beginning to affect his availability, especially with another game approaching.Thursday brought a much better update. According to the Chiefs' injury report, Kelce was a full participant, suggesting that he had made progress since the previous day. Rashee Rice and Niko Remigio also moved up to full participation after being limited on Wednesday.The change gives Kansas City a more positive outlook heading into the weekend. Unless Kelce suffers a setback or is downgraded significantly on Friday, he appears well positioned to play in Week 9.For Mahomes, having Kelce available is particularly important. The two have built a strong connection over several seasons, and the quarterback continues to rely on the tight end when the passing game needs a dependable option.Chiefs' reliance on Kelce raises questions about receiver depthTravis Kelce's importance to the offense is becoming harder to overlook. At 37, he remains one of Mahomes' most reliable targets during the 2026 season, even as the Chiefs continue to manage his ankle problem.His receiving numbers underline that value. Kelce has recorded at least 50 receiving yards in five of Kansas City's seven games. He has also reached the 40-yard mark in six of those seven outings.Those numbers make him a central part of the passing attack. They also highlight a potential concern for the Chiefs. If a tight end dealing with a lingering injury is leading the way among the team's receiving options, Kansas City may need more production from its wide receivers.That is one reason the Chiefs have reportedly considered adding a wide receiver before the trade deadline. A move could give Mahomes another dependable target and reduce the pressure on Kelce to carry such a large share of the passing game.Kansas City still has time to address that need. Kelce's Thursday update is encouraging, but one healthy practice does not erase the larger question surrounding the offense. The Chiefs need him on the field, yet they also need other receivers to step up if they want to make a serious push for another Super Bowl in 2026.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2023, Patrick Mahomes moved into his custom Missouri compound; the eight-acre estate shows how far he's come
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes moved his family into a custom-built compound in Belton, Missouri, in 2023, nearly three years after he bought the land.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes moved his family into a custom-built compound in Belton, Missouri, in 2023, nearly three years after he bought the land. He paid a reported $400,000 for eight empty acres in September 2020, weeks after the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback signed a 10-year, $450 million extension. The finished estate has a private football field, a par 3 golf hole, a pool and a pond. It also shows how a superstar can choose to put down roots in the city where he plays.How did Patrick Mahomes build his eight-acre Missouri estate?The timeline matters, so start there. Mahomes signed his extension with the Chiefs in August 2020. A month later he bought the Belton plot, which was listed through Loch Lloyd Residential Real Estate at $400,000. Outlets place it in Cass County, south of Kansas City, and the price and acreage are consistent across reports.He did not buy a finished mansion. He bought open land and then waited. Construction reportedly began around 2021. By July 2023, aerial photos shared online showed a completed house, and the family moved in that year. Nearly three years from purchase to move-in is a long stretch for a quarterback who played in two Super Bowls while it went up.Brittany Mahomes captured what the project meant to them. “Finally we’re gonna have a home that we built and has everything we could have ever dreamed of having,” she said.The goal was never to flip a trophy property. It was to design a place around the family’s real routines, one decision at a time.What is actually inside the Mahomes compound?The football field gets the headlines, and it earns them. It is a custom 50-yard field with Mahomes’ logo at midfield and his surname painted across the end zone. A soccer net sits at one end, so it works for more than one sport.The rest of the grounds read like a private resort. There is a par 3 golf hole, a pool, and a pond with a fountain. Front Office Sports listed those features when the aerial images surfaced, and other outlets repeated them.Inside, the look is clean and bright. Reports describe floor-to-ceiling sliding glass doors, white walls, glass partitions, white tile floors and a full gym. There is also dedicated space for his large shoe collection. Hello magazine put a value of about $8 million on the property, but that is an outside estimate. There is no official figure, and anyone quoting a precise number is guessing.What stands out is how much of it is built for use, not display. A field that size is a training tool as much as a flex. A gym at home means workouts happen without a commute, a camera or a crowd.Why Patrick Mahomes built in Missouri and not TexasMahomes does have a Texas base. He and Brittany bought a home in Westlake in March 2020 for $3.37 million, and he trains there in spring and summer. So why spend years and serious money on a second estate in Missouri?The answer is in what each home is for. Westlake is the offseason retreat. Belton is where the family lives during the season, close to the team that pays him.His earlier Kansas City homes show a steady climb. Reports say he bought a condo in December 2017 for about $350,000, then a three-bedroom house for $1.8 million in January 2019. Both have since been sold. Each purchase was bigger and more permanent than the last, and the compound is the first one built from scratch.That is my read, but the pattern is hard to miss. Building rather than buying is a long-term commitment. Nobody pours years into custom grounds near a team they plan to leave. For fans who worry about their quarterback’s loyalty, a private field in Belton says more than most press conferences.What the property says about Mahomes beyond footballLook at who the compound serves. Mahomes and Brittany have young children, and they often share small glimpses of home life online. A big field, a pool and open grass make sense for kids, not just for an athlete who needs to stay sharp.It also helps to see the money in proportion. The land cost about $400,000 against a $450 million contract, which is less than a tenth of one percent. Even if the total build cost is many times higher, the first purchase was a modest bet. The rest grew slowly over the next three years, which suggests patience more than splurging.The compound also solves a problem that famous athletes face. Privacy is hard to buy in a city that treats its quarterback as a neighbour and a hero. Eight acres with a field, a gym and a pool lets a family live loudly at home without leaving. Mahomes can throw, golf, swim and train within a few hundred yards of his own front door.None of this proves anything about his next contract or his future in Kansas City. But it does show what he values: space, routine and a base built to last. For a player whose job is to make chaos look calm, that may be the point.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Madrid: Lamine Yamal's locker and Kylian Mbappe's presence leaves NFL players starstruck as Cincinnati Bengals face Atlanta Falcons at Bernabeu
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins expressed his excitement over the prospect of Kylian Mbappe being at the Bernabeu to watch Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons; watch live coverage from Madrid on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm, with kickoff at 2.30pm
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals star Karrass revealed this week he has been using the locker of the Barcelona sensation while practicing at La Ciudad del Futbol, the Spain national team's training facility.

The NFL is back in Madrid for a second year running this week as the Bengals face the Atlanta Falcons at Real's iconic Bernabeu, live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm this Sunday.

"I think it's just because where the offensive line is," said Karrass of Lamine Yamal's locker. "Down the line. He's kind of in the middle over there, so it makes sense. It's a big honour.

"It was a fun summer watching the World Cup, and congrats to Spain for winning, and it's cool to be in the vicinity of world champions, which is what we aspire to be."

The game in Madrid follows on from the NFL's debut in Paris in representing the seventh of a record nine international games being played during the 2026 campaign, with Munich and Mexico City set to complete the slate later this month.

Madrid entered the fold as a host city this time last year when the Miami Dolphins beat the Washington Commanders, the league's return underlining its commitment to growing new markets and audiences overseas.

Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins welcomed the opportunity to travel to Europe as a landmark moment in his career, both from a personal and professional standpoint.

"Once I landed out here, I was just like, I can't believe I actually crossed the Atlantic," Higgins told reporters.

"It's my first time ever, you know, crossing the Atlantic into Europe. So it's just like it's amazing to me, you know what I mean? Just knowing where I came from and even bringing my family out here because it's their first time as well. So it's pretty dope. It's surreal."

Madrid star Kyle Mbappe has suggested he could be attendance for Sunday's game following Real's away fixture against Valencia on Saturday evening.

"It'd be dope to have him there," Higgins said. "I watch him on TV all the time. It's so crazy, bro. We was just talking about how fast this dude is, right? Like, how do you run that fast dribbling the ball on your feet? Like, that's crazy."

Falcons running back Bijan Robinson meanwhile said he plans to meet up with Vinícius Junior and Mbappe prior to Sunday's matchup, and on Thursday caught up with England midfielder Jude Bellingham.

Robinson explained that he met Vinicius through a mutual jeweller when Brazil played in the US some years back, while Mbappe spent time trying his hand at American football with Robinson during a promotional event last week.

The Falcons star leads the NFL with 780 rushing yards through eight weeks, but is without a 100-yard game over his last four outings.

"I've got to be better for this team. I've got to be better for the offense," he said. "Me and my running back coach, we always point this laser beam at the ceiling because we're always trying to play at the highest level. And for us, helping my team win games is us playing at the highest level."

articles.title: Ranking the Buffalo Bills' 10 Most Important Players for the Rest of 2026
articles.summary: A 53-man roster requires contributions from top to bottom, but not all roles are created equal.
articles.body:
A 53-man roster requires contributions from top to bottom, but not all roles are created equal.

Some key contributors are easier to replace than others, and a few can hit a midseason slump or miss a couple of games without derailing Buffalo's title aspirations.

As the Bills hit the midpoint as the league's Super Bowl favorite , these 10 players carry the heaviest weight on the roster.

The 29-year-old is the operational brain guiding the interior offensive line. He's critical to both a running game that was the league's best in 2025 and a passing game that has once again been dominant in 2026, and his are the last hands on the ball before perennial MVP candidate Josh Allen does his thing.

Allen and McGovern both essentially or fully sat out Week 18 in 2024 and 2025, outside of that, McGovern has been Allen's center in every game since sliding over to take that role in 2024.

The Bills have decent depth inside with veterans Lloyd Cushenberry and Austin Corbett on the roster, but extended time without McGovern would be a huge blow to the offense both on the ground and through the air.

Oftentimes, When Allen drops back to pass, right tackle Spencer Brown is the front-side anchor standing directly in his field of vision, tasked with washing away edge rushers looking to demolish QB1.

It's a big job, and one that Brown has held down in 75 of Allen's last 91 games.

At Pro Football Focus, Brown also earned a top-10 qualified grade at his position as a run blocker in both 2024 and 2025 . And while backup Tylan Grable did a respectable job in place of an injured Brown in Week 8, it wasn't a total coincidence that the offense looked out of sync most of the game without him.

If there's one player with the untapped ceiling to turn Buffalo from a contender into a champion, it's Kincaid. The talent is undeniable, and he has shown glimpses of domination the last few years.

Buffalo needs Kincaid to operate as that steady safety valve, taking defensive attention away from DJ Moore on the boundary, James Cook in the backfield, and Allen on designed runs and scrambles.

The 27-year-old earned his first Pro Bowl nod in 2025 and he's on pace to make a run at his first 1,000-yard campaign in 2026. He's right there.

The reigning rushing champion probably doesn't get enough credit for just how electric and consistently productive he's been since becoming a full-time starter in 2023.

Yes, ball security is sometimes a concern for the three-time Pro Bowler. And while that hurts him in award voting and fantasy rankings, it underscores the stakes: Buffalo needs Cook to keep defenses honest, but the offense can't afford careless giveaways on a Super Bowl run.

This entire offense runs through Allen, but keeping the engine humming starts with Dawkins, as it has for the vast majority of the quarterback's career.

You can count on one hand the number of games Allen has played without Dawkins protecting his blind side. The 32-year-old is a five-time Pro Bowler who has consistently been viewed as one of the strongest tackles in the sport.

With Grable already working in for Brown as the starting right tackle deals with a balky back, there is virtually no safety net for this offensive front without Dawkins anchoring the left side. And that's before even considering his emotional leadership as the heartbeat of this offense.

The top-graded pass-rusher on this defense at PFF this season isn't Greg Rousseau—it's Walker. In fact, the 22-year-old's 88.3 pass-rush grade leads all interior defensive linemen across the NFL.

Beyond that, he's stellar against the run and visibly improving each week. Walker doesn't look remotely green for a sophomore middle-round draft pick, and he's legitimately in the All-Pro conversation entering the heart of the season.

It's become increasingly difficult for the Bills to rely on the oft-injured Ed Oliver, leaving Walker as the centerpiece responsible for making plays and taking on multiple blockers to ease the burden on the team's higher-profile edge defenders.

Buffalo's secondary is often a liability, and Benford has experienced as many downs as ups thus far in 2026, but he indisputably remains the defense's No. 1 cover man. And there's a good chance the Bills would have lost at least one of the tilts on their current three-game winning streak if not for significant contributions from the 26-year-old.

Is he a star? No. Does he have that potential? Absolutely. But beyond that, his immense value stems from the harsh reality behind him: Buffalo's second-best corner right now is an unproven rookie, Davison Igbinosun. The team is waiting for offseason acquisition Dee Alford to become a reliable presence, and the coaching staff may have already given up on sophomore first-round pick Maxwell Hairston. That being the case, it's nearly impossible to envision Buffalo making a deep playoff run without high-level play from Benford down the stretch.

Meet the only player in the NFL this season with at least seven sacks and three forced fumbles.

Playing a redefined role in Jim Leonhard's new defense, Rousseau has exploded in his sixth season. On top of that splash production, he leads the league with 22 quarterback hits and has emerged as a reliable coverage defender when needed.

The 2021 first-round pick was always a solid pass rusher and strong run defender, but now it's all come together in his age-26 season. He has flat-out become one of the premier defensive disruptors in the league.

And the Bills are lucky for that, because veteran offseason addition Bradley Chubb has failed to produce consistently and there isn't a lot of depth on the edge in Buffalo.

Moore hasn't been healthy as often as the Bills need him to be this year, which goes a long way toward explaining why this unit has frequently looked out of rhythm despite the gaudy totals. Those who have watched this unit all season can see that a lot of points have been left on the field, which is both scary and an indication that the sky is the limit with Moore.

The 29-year-old vet forces defenses to use significant resources focusing on him, mainly because he can separate, and because he can win contested passes even when he doesn't. It's a luxury the Bills rarely had after parting ways with Stefon Diggs earlier this decade, and now we've seen guys like Kincaid, Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir benefit mightily from that dynamic.

The volume and consistency aren't quite there yet as Moore works through injuries, but the impact has already been tremendous and the value is immeasurable.

I mean, does this require an explanation? Allen remains the definitive favorite to win his second MVP award in what has been a superhero season to date. Empirically and on tape, he's the best quarterback—if not the most dominant player, period—in football today.

With him, they're the favorite to win Super Bowl LXI. Without him, they wouldn't be a playoff team.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes marks a new development in Kansas City as their foundation helps restaurants become safer for people with allergies
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have been a driving force behind a number of developments in Kansas
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have been a driving force behind a number of developments in Kansas City. Through their foundation, 15 and Mahomies, both Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have continued to serve different communities. Ahead of the match against the New York Jets, the popular social media influencer Brittany Mahomes has shared a new milestone that their milestone achieved recently.Patrick Mahomes' wife, Brittany Mahomes, makes an update about their foundation’s recent milestone in Kansas CityA few hours ago, Patrick Mahomes' wife, Brittany Mahomes took to her social media to make a post about how a restaurant in Kansas City has brought in changes for people with allergies. This is related to their foundation’s recent project where they are collaborating with restaurants to train them to deal with allergies.The post reads as, “Watch how an allergy order moves through @joeskc —from the counter to the kitchen to the table. Joe’s is the first restaurant to earn FARE Approved Restaurant Partner recognition through 15 and FARE, the initiative of FARE and 15 and the Mahomies Foundation.⁠”The post added, “The Joe’s team completed FARE’s food allergy training to help prevent allergic reactions and to know how to respond if one happens. Any restaurant can do this—and through 15 and FARE, Kansas City-area restaurants complete it at no cost.⁠ ⁠More than 10 Kansas City restaurants and bakeries are close behind.”For the unversed, 15 and FARE is a joint initiative launched by 15 and the Mahomies Foundation and FARE (Food Allergy Research & Education) to improve food allergy awareness, reduce care inequities in marginalized communities, and create safer dining and community spaces in Kansas City.The organisations provide Food Allergy Academy training and anaphylaxis (severe allergic reaction) response training for local restaurants, food banks, and pantries.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ children are the reason behind this noble initiative in Kansas CityWhile it is a noble cause, Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes also have a personal story related to the initiative.Their children, Sterling and Bronze, have severe allergies which has helped the star player Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes learn more about the triggers and what they can do to prevent it.In many of their interviews, Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have been emotional about how it was tough dealing with their children's allergies since neither of them faced it in their childhoods.Since it came as a shock, Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, were not equipped well to deal with it and this helped them to launch a new initiative through their foundation to help more and more adults and children dealing with the same condition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Derrick Henry Addresses NFL Trade Rumors After Ravens' Loss to Jaguars on TNF
articles.summary: Having lost four consecutive games, including three straight by at least 22 points, Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry isn't concerning himself with what might happen before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.body:
Having lost four consecutive games, including three straight by at least 22 points, Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry isn't concerning himself with what might happen before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Speaking to reporters after the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night, Henry was asked about his status with the organization ahead of the deadline.

"I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around.'"

Henry's name hadn't really popped up as a trade candidate because it was assumed the return of Lamar Jackson would elevate the Ravens back to being a playoff contender in the AFC.

Instead, Jackson's uncertain status for the remainder of the season after suffering a thumb injury on his first pass attempt in Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills might have Baltimore rethinking its plans.

ESPN's Dan Graziano cited Henry as a player to watch on the running-back market leading up to Tuesday's trade deadline.

However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said on Friday's episode of Good Morning Football that the Ravens' acquisition of Jacoby Brissett makes it less likely they will be deadline sellers with the hope he can keep them above water with a more talented roster around him than he had in Arizona.

One issue with that line of thinking, though, is the Ravens haven't been playing up to their talent level outside of the quarterback conundrum. They rank 26th in points allowed per game.

Advanced metrics are a little more kind to Baltimore's defense, which is ranked 18th in both EPA per play and success rate. The Ravens have been outscored 104-33 in the last three games.

Henry does have one more year on his contract after this season, so perhaps Baltimore is also thinking ahead to 2027 with a healthy Jackson. He has a $16.3 million cap hit next season, but Baltimore would save $12 million if he were to be moved.

Another potential issue is would Henry bring back enough in a trade to make it worth making a move. He is a 32-year-old running back on an expensive contract and is averaging a career-low 3.9 yards per carry.

Since Week 1 when he ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns against the Indianapolis Colts, Henry has 545 yards and five touchdowns in eight games.

articles.title: Week 9 Waiver Wire Pickups, Best Fantasy Sleepers to Target After Box Score Review
articles.summary: Week 9 got underway with Thursday night's matchup between the Baltimore Ravens and Jacksonville Jaguars. Baltimore was forced to dig deep into its quarterback depth chart because of injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, which was an obvious problem.
articles.body:
Week 9 got underway with Thursday night's matchup between the Baltimore Ravens and Jacksonville Jaguars. Baltimore was forced to dig deep into its quarterback depth chart because of injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, which was an obvious problem.

Likewise, many fantasy managers may face problematic situations in Week 9 because of injuries and/or bye weeks. The Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans have the week off. Late-developing situations, like Garrett Wilson landing in the concussion protocol , could be particularly problematic because waivers have been processed in most leagues.

A few viable starters may still be available, though. Here, you'll find a look at the top late-week waiver targets for point-per-reception (PPR) play.

Malik Willis has started to settle in as the Miami Dolphins' starting quarterback, and he looks far more comfortable as a passer than he did at the beginning of the season.

The talented dual-threat only ran once against the New England Patriots last week, but he tossed a pair of touchdowns and tallied 15.6 fantasy points. He ran eight times in each of his previous two games and topped 20 fantasy points in each of them.

Despite Willi's recent success, he's still only rostered in 27 percent of leagues. He's worth adding and starting this week, and he has a favorable stretch of matchups upcoming.

It starts with this week's game against the Detroit Lions, who have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing QBs than any other team.

The Cleveland Browns have placed quarterback Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol ahead of their matchup with the New Orleans Saints. That probably doesn't bode well for most of Cleveland's skill players. It could, however, be good for Browns receiving back Dylan Sampson.

Assuming Todd Monken tries to get Shedeur Sanders some easy completions early, Sampson is likely to have a large workload. He's also played a prolific role since returning from an early-season injury and has been targeted 11 times over the past two weeks.

Sampson has caught all 11 of those passes while rushing for 52 yards. He has reached double-digit fantasy points in each of his two appearances this season. He'll have a good chance to do it again in New Orleans this week.

The Saints have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing receivers than any other team through Week 8. Sampson is rostered in 22 percent of leagues.

While Willis and Sampson both face favorable matchups in Week 9, that won't be the case for Jets receiver Adonai Mitchell. New York has a road matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs, who have surrendered the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers.

Yet, Mitchell could see enough volume to reward managers as a sleeper flex play. With Wilson out, Geno Smith is likely to target Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. early and often.

Cooper finished Week 8 without a catch, but Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown. He's highly unlikely to match the 27.2 fantasy points he delivered last week, but Mitchell should have a reasonable PPR floor.

Mitchell is rostered in only 34 percent of leagues heading into the weekend.

As Willis has settled into Miami's starting role, he's also done a nice job of getting tight end Greg Dulcich involved. Dulcich has been targeted at least five times in each of his last three games and he has topped eight fantasy points in each of them.

Dulcich was held without a catch by the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4, but he has caught at least four passes and topped eight fantasy points in four of his last five games. He should again approach double digits against the Lions.

Detroit can score points in bunches, which will likely mean opportunities for Miami's pass catchers. The Lions have also struggled to limit opposing tight ends and have surrendered an average of 23.6 fantasy points to the position.

No team has allowed more fantasy points to tight ends than Detroit. Dulcich is only rostered in eight percent of fantasy leagues.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson Was Hospitalized for 'Medical Emergency' After 'Neurological Symptoms'
articles.summary: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson was recently hospitalized after "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency."
articles.body:
New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson was recently hospitalized after "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency."

In a statement released on Friday, Henderson said he was hospitalized for several days after experiencing "neurological symptoms" that led to him undergoing comprehensive medical testing that came back "positive and reassuring" even though the root cause of the issue is "unknown and unexplainable."

articles.title: Mike McDaniel making 1 major change amid Chargers’ struggles
articles.summary: McDaniel is searching for answers after an 0-7 start
articles.body:
Mike McDaniel was supposed to be the savior for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers' offense. His motion- and timing-heavy scheme made the world think Tua Tagovailoa was a functional NFL quarterback, yet somehow Herbert and Co. are completely unraveling early into their partnership.

The Chargers are comfortably the NFL's lowest-scoring team at 14.7 points per game, Herbert leads the league in interceptions with 10, and running back Omarion Hampton is facing catastrophic second-year regression.

In short, nothing is working. So, McDaniel is making a major change on game days: moving from the sideline to the booth.

"Seems like a good action to take based on how things have gone this year," McDaniel said , "and realistically something that I've only brought up because I've observed, I'm very confident in the rest of the offensive coaching staff and how they're able to set the tone and communicate information on the sidelines.

So, I feel a little more comfortable to try that."

Perhaps this gives the Chargers offense a spark, but it reeks of rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. Nevertheless, Los Angeles hopes to avoid falling to 0-8 Sunday against the Houston Texans .

articles.title: Packers Addition Makes Honest Admission About Position Change
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers surprisingly started offensive lineman Laken Tomlinson at right guard in Week 8 despite having one start on that side of the offensive...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers surprisingly started offensive lineman Laken Tomlinson at right guard in Week 8 despite having one start on that side of the offensive line in his 12-year NFL career.

Tomlinson noted that the transition is going great, but it was a lot tougher last week given the short week and lack of practice time.

"I mean, it's definitely a challenge, especially last week," admitted Tomlinson.

Tomlinson started for the Packers at left guard in Week 7. So, he practiced on the left side leading up to the game.

Green Bay Packers Guard Laken Tomlinson Opens Up on Changing Sides

Because the Packers played on Thursday night in Week 8, the team did not have a legitimate practice. So, Tomlinson had to change sides without much work in team drills. Tomlinson noted that the flip side is that this week gives him extra time to prepare for staying on the right side.

"This week, especially going into the long weekend, I had some extra time to kind of just like go over some stuff on my own," said Tomlinson. "Work on my technique and just work on flipping things technique-wise, and having these two days of practice. So definitely a lot more comfortable now."

Tomlinson has 11,131 snaps at left guard in his NFL career. After his Week 8 start, he has 131 snaps at right guard. The Packers coaching staff noted that Tomlinson was playing so well that they could not bench him.

However, with starter Aaron Banks back in the lineup, the team could not keep him on the left side. So, they started him at right guard.

Tomlinson has done well in pass protection, but the run game has not been seeing the benefits of the offensive line changes. The Packers guard noted that the team needs to stick with the ground attack and not give up now.

"It's coming, man," said Tomlinson. "You just got to have faith and keep chopping wood. There's the old saying, just like keep chopping wood. And you know, keep feeding the ball, keep running the ball, and you'll see it come. I promise."

It is fair that Tomlinson made his first start at right guard and Banks made his first start since Week 2. Meanwhile, Josh Jacobs has only played two games as the Packers' running back. An improved and more consistent offensive line, combined with Jacobs feeling more comfortable behind the line, could lead to an improved rushing attack.

The results have not shown yet, but there is reason to have hope towards the end of the season. The Packers will head to New England to take on the Patriots in Week 9.

articles.title: Ravens make unwanted NFL history in 33-10 loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: Joe Fagnano's debut, unusual Derrick Henry nuggets and several Ravens trends stood out in Baltimore's loss to the Jaguars.
articles.body:
Joe Fagnano had a chance to make a little history Thursday night as QB1 for the Baltimore Ravens . The former UConn Huskies quarterback entered his first NFL start with a chance to end a long jinx.

A win would make him the first quarterback from the program to win an NFL game as a starter in nearly 15 full years . The last person to do so? Dan Orlovsky did it with the Indianapolis Colts in 2011. Orlovsky led Indianapolis to victories over the Houston Texans and Tennessee Titans that December. Let's say that unfortunate streak will have to continue a little longer.

Fagnano and the Ravens had a tough night, and the rookie's difficult debut as a starter ended with 10 completions on 18 attempts for 60 yards. He threw zero touchdown passes, two interceptions, and notched a 22.7 passer rating.

The Jacksonville Jaguars handed the Ravens a 33-10 defeat . Baltimore's losing streak stretches to four games. The loss offered plenty to examine beyond the final score, including some unusual personnel usage and a few trends that should concern Baltimore moving forward.

Derrick Henry had an unusual night under center

Derrick Henry has been used in the Wildcat formation before, but Thursday night's workload was something else. Per Ryan Mink, via Pro Football Focus, he entered the game with eight Wildcat snaps this season and added 10 more against Jacksonville. Per PFF, Henry had never taken more than five snaps at quarterback in a game before this season, with that previous career high dating back to 2018.

Another amusing detail: Henry has thrown more career touchdown passes than Baltimore's current quarterback room combined. That's not exactly the kind of statistical distinction an offense wants to advertise, but it speaks to how unusual the Ravens' quarterback situation has become. With Jackson and Huntley unavailable, Baltimore has had to get creative, even if asking its star running back to take on more quarterback responsibilities isn't a sustainable solution

The Ravens made franchise history for all the wrong reasons

The 33-10 defeat extended a particularly ugly offensive trend. Baltimore has now been held below 14 points in four consecutive games. Jamison Hensley reports that's the first time that has happened in franchise history. That's a remarkable distinction for an organization that has traditionally built its identity around physical football and an offense that can control games.

The penalty situation has become just as concerning. Baltimore committed three false starts in the first half and finished with four against Jacksonville. That brings the Ravens' season total to an NFL-worst 24. As Hensley also reports, they have already surpassed the 19 false starts they committed across all 17 games in 2025.

Ravens find themselves on the wrong end of a Liam Coen benchmark

Andrew Whitworth revealed on the Prime Video Postgame Show that the Jaguars have now scored 702 points in 25 games under head coach Liam Coen, and that only two head coaches, Mike Martz and Sean McVay, reached that scoring benchmark faster.

That's an impressive milestone for a coach who has helped transform Jacksonville's offensive identity. The Jaguars have found ways to generate points consistently, and Thursday's performance showed how difficult they can be to contain when Lawrence and Coen are operating comfortably.

For Baltimore, the benchmark is another reminder of the offensive firepower it must contend with in the AFC. Jacksonville isn't simply enjoying one productive afternoon. Its scoring output under Coen reflects sustained offensive production that makes the Jaguars a difficult matchup for opposing defenses.

Kyle Hamilton continues adding to his defensive legacy

Even in another disappointing Ravens performance, Kyle Hamilton continued demonstrating why he's considered one of the NFL's most versatile defensive players. His ability to line up in different roles and affect plays near the line of scrimmage separates him from most safeties.

According to PFF, Hamilton leads all NFL safeties in tackles for loss or no gain this season with 10. Jalen Ramsey is second with seven, followed by Cooper DeJean with six and Tykee Smith with five.

That versatility is particularly valuable for a defense dealing with injuries and inconsistent performances elsewhere. Hamilton can contribute against the run, pressure the quarterback, and work in coverage, giving Baltimore a defender capable of filling multiple responsibilities.

He left this one with an injury , and the Ravens will certainly hope he can get back on the field as quickly as possible. His continued production is one of the few dependable positives the Ravens can take from an otherwise miserable stretch.

articles.title: Dianna Russini Set to Return to Media: What We Know
articles.summary: Russini’s new content is expected to be sponsored by gambling operators.
articles.body:
Dianna Russini is poised to make a sports media comeback soon, Front Office Sports has confirmed, several months after resigning from The Athletic in the aftermath of Page Six publishing photos showing her with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at an adults-only Arizona resort in April.

After ProFootballTalk first reported that Russini has told people around the NFL that she is expecting to return to the industry next week, several options have emerged for what comes next.

Russini is expected to launch new content sponsored by gambling operators, sources said, adding that there have been talks with Jake Paul's Betr platform as well as offshore sportsbook BetUS. One source said that Russini has also had talks with iHeart.

FOS discovered a new X/Twitter page titled "Russini Report," created in October, that only has three followers—Andres Vargas, a content creator and spokesperson for BetUS, and Crossing Lines, a show sponsored by BetUS featuring ex-Barstool personality Jeff Nadu and co-host Donnie Seymour. An additional video manager, named Natalie, also follows the page from a protected account. The "Russini Report" page indicates a show will air live on Wednesdays encompassing pro football news, injuries, and analysis. The page previously indicated the show would be "powered by BetUS," but that language has since been edited out.

Basketball Hall of Famer Dennis Rodman is also an endorser of BetUS, which is headquartered in Costa Rica.

On Wednesday, Page Six reported that Russini will be "headlining her own show" on a digital platform. "It's been in the works for a while and she can't wait to get back to what she loves," a source told Page Six .

Russini stopped responding to messages when presented with BetUS, Betr, and iHeart as places she has had talks with. Her agent, Matt Olson of CAA, referred FOS to the publicist Melissa Nathan, who declined to comment. Spokespeople for BetUS, Betr, and iHeart did not respond to requests for comment, nor did Vargas.

Jon "Stugotz" Weiner, a host for iHeart and its subsidiary Fox Sports Radio, has previously said he would welcome the chance to collaborate with Russini again. Russini was a frequent guest on Weiner's previous show, The Dan Le Batard Show With Stugotz , and also joined Weiner on his I Love Football show during Super Bowl week this past February. If Russini reaches a deal with iHeart, it is not expected to encompass Fox Sports Radio, one source said.

Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy also previously said he would consider hiring Russini, but he told FOS this week that she is not going to work for Barstool now. Sources told FOS that Kalshi, Underdog, and FanDuel are not in the running to sponsor her content at this time.

After Russini and Vrabel were photographed hugging and holding hands, the two issued statements saying that their relationship was platonic, not romantic. Russini resigned from the New York Times -owned Athletic about a week later, and Vrabel missed one day of the NFL Draft to attend counseling.

One source told FOS he expects Russini to lean into her NFL Insider role. The question is how much cooperation she will get from NFL players and coaches, as well as the league itself, with the NFL playoffs and Super Bowl only months away. "All she needs is one big scoop to show she has motion," says the source.

In September, The Athletic released an investigation saying that Russini "should have disclosed to The Athletic the nature of her relationship with [Mike] Vrabel to allow editors to assess the kinds of stories on which she should have been working."

The investigation did not seek to discover whether the two had a romantic relationship, and while it noted that Russini was "effusive" in her praise of Vrabel at times, it mirrored how he was covered by other outlets.

Ultimately, the investigation recommended editor's notes be added to three videos and one story in which Russini covered Vrabel during her time at The Athletic .
authors: Ryan Glasspiegel, Mark Maske and Michael McCarthy

articles.title: Rashee Rice files bankruptcy despite having $6M in career earnings
articles.summary: The Chiefs’ WR is filing for bankruptcy at 26-years-old.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has a penchant for making headlines, and he's done so once more by filing for bankruptcy in the Northern District of Texas. Rice is claiming that he has $3.45M in unpaid debts — despite having career earnings of $6M, and being on the verge of getting the first major payday of his career as he 26-year-old is set to hit free agency in 2027.

A variety of legal issues are cited as the core reason for Rice's financial troubles. Court documents obtained by ESPN show that Rice is claiming that he has just over $13,000 in his checking account, and $677K in personal assets — while owing just over $1.8M in outstanding settlements from lawsuits, as well as outstanding legal fees. In addition, Rice doesn't own any property and still rents — while also noting that he used his Super Bowl ring as collateral for legal fees. The breakdown in the documents are as following:

$979,837 outstanding from a settlement in the 2024 car accident caused by Rice in Dallas that resulted in the receiver pleading guilty to one count of collision involving serious bodily injury and one count of racing on a highway causing bodily injury.

$700,000 from two other victims in the same accident

$200,000 from a civil suit filed in February by Rice's ex-girlfriend, alleging physical and emotional abuse.

It's unclear who the remaining debt money is owed to, totaling approximately $2M.

Rice's NFL future is likely assured, because when on the field, he has been a difference-maker — which should enable him to receive another contract, one that will be substantially larger than his rookie deal. That said, the litany of off-field issues will ensure he will not earn what he could have made on the market without legal trouble. Rice was most recently sentenced to a 30-day jail sentence in Dallas over the Summer for testing positive for THC, is violation of his probation stemming from the 2024 car accident.

Now the 26-year-old is financially underwater, his Super Bowl ring isn't in his possession, and he seemingly has nothing to show for earning $6M over the last four years.

articles.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Matchups to Exploit: Patriots, Dolphins have multiple players in good spots
articles.summary: Ray Garvin takes you through five players who have matchups they can exploit in Week 9 for fantasy football.
articles.body:
We're into Week 9 of the fantasy football season and plenty of new names have emerged as assets. With that, we have to evaluate which players are in the best spots. That's where Ray Garvin comes in with his matchups to exploit for fantasy football in Week 9.

I'm buying into Jonah Coleman this week, and I think there's a real chance he finishes as an RB1 against Carolina.

Coleman got his opportunity with RJ Harvey on injured reserve and made the most of it. He handled 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City, adding four catches for 63 yards on five targets. More importantly, he out-touched J.K. Dobbins 15-7 and played nearly 68% of Denver's offensive snaps. He also ran 17 routes on 34 dropbacks. That's not just a rookie getting a few designed touches. That's a running back earning a role.

Now, he gets a Panthers defense allowing 28.3 full-PPR points per game to opposing backfields, second-most in the NFL. Carolina is surrendering 4.73 yards per carry and has already given up 10 rushing touchdowns. Since Week 4, opposing lead backs have averaged roughly 20 PPR points per game against them.

That's the part that makes this matchup so appealing. Coleman doesn't need 20 carries to beat his ranking. If he's getting double-digit rushes, involved in the passing game and seeing valuable touches near the goal line, the ceiling is there.

He's RB16 in half-PPR consensus, but I'm comfortable starting him as an RB2 with legitimate top-12 upside. I don't expect Dobbins to disappear, but this looks like Coleman's backfield to lead right now.

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, Patriots vs. Packers

Rhamondre Stevenson is another running back I'm willing to push up my rankings, especially if TreVeyon Henderson misses another game.

With Henderson out last week, Stevenson carried the ball 19 times for 82 yards and added three receptions. The other Patriots' backs combined for nine carries. That's the type of workload we want to see, even if there wasn't a touchdown attached to it.

Green Bay has allowed 25.0 full-PPR points per game to opposing backfields, seventh-most in the league. An opposing running back has scored at least 13 PPR points against the Packers in four straight games. That's not a defense I'm treating as a shutdown matchup for the position.

There's also a physicality element here. Stevenson has shown the ability to make defenders miss, while Green Bay has struggled to limit yards after contact recently. If New England keeps giving him opportunities, he can create something even when the initial blocking isn't perfect.

The receiving work matters, too. Stevenson has 23 catches on the season, so he isn't entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to help your lineup. He's also averaging just 3.8 yards per carry, which makes that additional volume even more important.

Henderson missed Wednesday and Thursday practices with an illness. We still need the final injury designation, but if he's out, Stevenson is a strong RB2 for me with top-12 upside. He's RB15 in consensus, and the workload could push him past that.

DeMario Douglas, WR, Patriots vs. Packers

We need to talk about DeMario Douglas, because there's an actual opportunity here if A.J. Brown misses another game.

Douglas led New England with 76 receiving yards last week, catching all three of his targets and scoring on a 48-yard touchdown. He's now scored four touchdowns over his past four games and topped 65 receiving yards in three of them.

Now, am I telling you three targets are enough to feel comfortable? Absolutely not. That's the concern. One big play carried his Week 8 production, and we can't just assume he's going to score every Sunday.

But the matchup gives us something to work with. Green Bay is allowing 34.8 full-PPR points per game to opposing wide receiver groups, ninth-most in the NFL. If Brown remains out, Douglas has a chance to operate as one of Drake Maye's primary passing-game options.

Keeping it real here, the Packers have been tougher on slot receivers than those overall numbers suggest. This isn't a free square. Green Bay has also been good at limiting explosive passes, so the targets may need to grow if Douglas is going to hit.

Still, with Brown and Hunter Henry both missing practice Wednesday and Thursday, it's reasonable to expect New England to lean on the weapons it has available.

Douglas is WR31 in half-PPR consensus. I'm comfortable with him as a flex play, especially if I need upside. Just understand that the ceiling is more attractive than the floor.

If you're streaming quarterbacks, Malik Willis is somebody I'm willing to take a shot on this week.

Detroit is allowing 24.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks, the most in the NFL. And this isn't just one ugly game skewing the numbers. Every quarterback the Lions have faced has finished QB13 or better, and they've allowed multiple passing touchdowns in every game.

Now, look at Willis. He's thrown two touchdowns in each of his past two starts, including 211 passing yards against New England last week. He also has 225 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns on the season. When the passing production and rushing production hit in the same game, he can give you a real difference-making fantasy performance.

But here's the part we can't ignore: Detroit can get after the quarterback.

The Lions are averaging 3.4 sacks per game, second-most in the league, while Miami has allowed pressure on 42.9% of dropbacks. Willis was sacked five times last week. That's a real concern and the biggest reason I'm not calling him a locked-in QB1.

Still, a quarterback who can create with his legs facing a defense that has consistently surrendered touchdowns is exactly the kind of streamer I'm interested in.

Willis is QB13 in consensus. I think he has a path to a top-10 finish, and if you're choosing between fringe starters this week, I'm leaning into the upside.

Greg Dulcich might be my favorite tight end streamer this week, and it's not just because Detroit has been awful against the position.

The usage is moving in the right direction.

Across his past three games, Dulcich has earned a 20% target share and a 25.5% first-read share while running a route on 62.6% of Miami's dropbacks. He's also averaging 2.68 yards per route run over that stretch. Those aren't empty routes. He's getting open, getting targeted and producing when the ball comes his way.

He's caught 13 passes for 166 yards in those three games without scoring a touchdown. Last week, he saw six targets and turned them into four catches for 43 yards.

Detroit is allowing 27.9 full-PPR points per game to tight ends, the most in football. Through seven games, the Lions have surrendered 11 receiving touchdowns to the position. Over their past five games, they've also allowed the most receiving fantasy points per game and the third-most yards per target to tight ends.

That's exactly what I'm looking for when streaming a tight end: a player earning opportunities against a defense giving up efficiency and touchdowns at the position.

Dulcich is TE17 in half-PPR consensus. I'm willing to start him over some of the usual low-end TE1 options. I think he's got a legitimate chance to finish inside the top 12, and one touchdown could turn this into a really good week.

articles.title: New York Giants' playoff fate will be heavily influenced by Eagles game
articles.summary: Is Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles a "must-win" for the New York Giants?
articles.body:
The New York Giants have a huge opportunity down in Philadelphia this Sunday

There's no such thing as a "must-win" in Week 9 of the NFL, but the Giants and their fans should ignore that. A lot is at stake in this game against the battered Eagles .

Based on the analytics and percentages, a Giants win would put them in prime position for a playoff spot. A loss would drop them back deep into the pack.

A Giants win would give them a 68 percent chance to win the NFC East and a 71 percent shot at making the playoffs.

A loss would lessen their division odds to 41 percent and their postseason odds to 43 percent. So, this is kind of a "must-win" for Big Blue (4-2-1) as their schedule gets dicey in the second half of the season.

The Giants have some tough games coming up the rest of the way. Keep in mind, they haven't yet played a team with a winning record and won't until Week 11, when the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars invade MetLife Stadium.

The schedule also has a home game against San Francisco and trips to Detroit and Seattle, all top contenders to win the NFC this year.

articles.title: 49ers DE Nick Bosa’s own words foreshadow Week 9 injury return vs. Raiders
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are set to be without wide receiver Mike Evans for Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders. However, they are likely to get a key defens...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are set to be without wide receiver Mike Evans for Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders. However, they are likely to get a key defensive star back in Nick Bosa .

Per NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Bosa has been back on the training field and believes he is finally ready to return after a lengthy layoff.

"Nick Bosa appears poised to return to the field for the first time since late September. Nick Bosa, dealing with a calf strain for about a month and a half. A little more for Nick Bosa. Calf strains are bad, they can linger. The 49ers know they are in it for the long haul. They wanted to make sure they take their time. But he has been on the field this week after the bye and told reporters in the locker room he believes he is good to go," Rapoport said.

A five-time Pro Bowler and one-time Defensive Player of the Year, Bosa is coming off a torn ACL that limited him to just three games last season. That is likely why the Niners have chosen to be a bit more cautious in treating Bosa's calf issue.
